InAnIdealWorld.description: Corrects `in ideal world` to `in an ideal world`.

InAnyWay.description: Corrects ungrammatical `in anyway` to `in any way`.

IncludingButNotLimitedToPunctuation.description: Adds the conventional commas around `including, but not limited to,` when used parenthetically.

Instead.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `instead`.

Insurmountable.description: Suggests the more standard and common synonym `insurmountable`.

Intact.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `intact`.

JetpackNames.description: Ensure proper capitalization of Jetpack-related terms.

Keystroke.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `keystroke`.

Keystrokes.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `keystrokes`.

KindSortOf.description: Flags `kind if` or `sort off` that stand before qualifiers so the filler `of` stays intact.

Koreas.description: When referring to the nations, make sure to treat them as a proper noun.

LessWorse.description: Suggests alternatives to `less/least worse/worst` for more standard, clearer comparisons.

Lifetime.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `lifetime`.

LookDownOnesNose.description: Corrects `look one's nose down` to `look down one's nose`

Lots.description: A collection of linters that can be run as one.

Malaysia.description: When referring to the states of Malaysia and their capitals, make sure to treat them as a proper noun.

MassExodus.description: Corrects the eggcorn `max exodues` to the idiomatic `mass exodus`.

Proofread.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `proofread`.

ProperNouns.description: Ensure proper capitalization of proper nouns.

QuantifierNeedsOf.description: Detects missing `of` after the quantifier “a couple” when it precedes a plural noun

QuiteMany.description: Corrects `quite many` to `quite a few`, which is the more natural and idiomatic phrase in standard English. `Quite many` is considered nonstandard usage.

QuoteSpacing.description: Checks that quotation marks are preceded or succeeded by whitespace.

RainbowColoredHyphen.description: When rainbow-colored or cream-colored describe a noun, replace the space between the color words with a hyphen to keep the modifier cohesive.

RallyToReally.description: Catches the typo where `rally` sneaks into `be + ...ing` constructions, including common contractions.

ReadsAndWrites.description: Corrects inconsistent noun or verb forms when `read` and `write` are paired.

RealTrouper.description: Ensures the correct use of `real trouper`, distinguishing it from `trooper`, which refers to a soldier or police officer.

ReasonForDoing.description: Corrects `reason of doing` to `reason for doing` etc.

RedundantAcronyms.description: Identifies redundant acronyms where the last word repeats the last letter's meaning (e.g., `ATM machine` → `ATM` or `automated teller machine`).

RedundantFirsts.description: Looks for redundant use of `first` with verbs that already imply order.

RedundantIIRC.description: Flags redundant use of 'if' or 'correctly' with `IIRC`, since `IIRC` already stands for 'if I recall correctly'.

RedundantPretty.description: `Pretty` is redundant when modifying `decent`. Use `decent` alone.

RedundantProgressiveComparative.description: Detects redundant comparatives like `increasingly more` and `increasingly less`.

RedundantSelf.description: Detects redundant use of `self-` prefixes with reflexive pronouns (e.g., `self-host it themselves`).

RedundantSuperlatives.description: Simplifies redundant double positives like `most optimal` to the base form.

RedundantThat.description: There is rarely a situation where `that that` cannot be condensed into a single token.

Regardless.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `regardless`.

RegimenRegiment.description: Corrects mistaken use of `regiment` (military unit) when `regimen` (routine) was intended.

RegularIrregulars.description: Replaces wrong regular inflections of words with their correct irregular forms.

RelayOnForRely.description: Corrects the frequent typo where `relay` is used in place of `rely` in the phrase `relay on`.

RepeatedWords.description: This rule looks for repetitions of words that are not homographs.

Respond.description: Flags uses of the noun `response` where the verb `respond` is needed after an auxiliary.

ResponsibilityFor.description: Corrects `take/assume/claim responsibility of` to `take/assume/claim responsibility for`.

RifeWith.description: Corrects `ripe with` to `rife with`, preserving the phrase’s meaning of being filled with something, often undesirable.

RiseTheQuestion.description: Corrects `rise the question` to `raise the question`.

RiseTheRanks.description: Corrects the nonstandard phrase `rise the ranks` to the standard `rise through the ranks` or `rise from the ranks`

RoadMap.description: Detects when `roadmap` is used instead of `road map`, prompting the correct spacing.

RollerSkated.description: Encourages hyphenating the past tense of `roller-skate`.

RulesOfThumb.description: Corrects pluralizing the wrong noun in `rule of thumb`.

RunIntoProblemsOrTrouble.description: Corrects `running into` `problems` or `trouble` with wrong article, singular, or plural forms.

SafeToSave.description: Detects `safe` (adjective) when `save` (verb) is intended after modal verbs like `could` or `should`.

SameAs.description: Corrects the incorrect phrase `same then` to the standard `same as`.

SaveToSafe.description: Corrects `save to <verb>` to `safe to <verb>` after a form of `be`.

ScantilyClad.description: Fixes `scandally clad` to `scantily clad`, ensuring clarity in describing minimal attire.

ScapeGoat.description: Corrects `scape goat` to `scapegoat`, which is the proper term for a person blamed for others' failures.

SeamToSeem.description: Corrects `seam` to `seem` when used as a verb meaning `to appear` or `to give the impression`.

SeizeControlOf.description: Corrects `seize control over` to `seize control of`.

SendAnEmailTo.description: Replaces the verbose phrase `send an email to` with the concise verb `email`.

SentenceCapitalization.description: The opening word of a sentence should almost always be capitalized.

SetABadExample.description: Corrects `set up a bad example` to `set a bad example`.

ShootOneselfInTheFoot.description: Corrects nonstandard variants of 'shoot oneself in the foot'.

Shortcoming.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `shortcoming`.

Shortcomings.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `shortcomings`.

ShutdownVerb.description: Keeps `shutdown` as a noun when it stands alone but swaps it for the phrasal verb `shut down` whenever an auxiliary precedes it.

SideTangent.description: Corrects redundant `side tangent` and `side tangents` to more concise alternatives.

SimilarLike.description: The adjective 'similar' pairs with the preposition 'to', so never follow it with 'like'.

SimpleGrammatical.description: Corrects `simply grammatical` to `simple grammatical` for proper adjective usage.

SimplePastToPastParticiple.description: Corrects simple past tense verbs to past participle after auxiliary verbs like "have" or "be".

SinceDuration.description: Detects the use of 'since' with a duration instead of a point in time.

SingleBe.description: Removes adjacent duplicate inflections of `be`, including contracted forms followed by another `be` verb.

Skyrocket.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `skyrocket`.

SneakPeekPreview.description: Corrects the common phrase-level confusion where `peak` is used instead of `peek` after `sneak`.

SomeOfThe.description: Quantity words such as `some` normally take `of` before a definite article. Including `of` signals that you mean a subset of a larger set, preventing a momentary stumble in comprehension.

SomeWithoutArticle.description: Detects the redundant article in front of `some` and suggests more natural phrasing.

Somebody.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `somebody`.

SomebodyElses.description: Corrects `somebody else's` when the `'s` is in the wrong place.

Somehow.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `somehow`.

Someone.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `someone`.

SomethingIs.description: Flags forms like `somethings` before progressive verbs and suggests using `something's` or `something is`.

SomewhatSomething.description: Flags the phrase `somewhat of a` in favor of `something of a`, which can be considered more traditional.

Somewhere.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `somewhere`.

SoonToBe.description: Hyphenates `soon-to-be` when it appears before a noun.

SoonerOrLater.description: Fixes the improper phrase `sooner than later` by suggesting standard alternatives.

Spaces.description: Words should be separated by at most one space.

SpellCheck.description: Looks and provides corrections for misspelled words.

SpelledNumbers.description: Most style guides recommend that you spell out numbers less than ten.

SpinalChord.description: The words `spinal`, `vocal`, `umbilical`, and `electrical` are followed by `cord`, so replace accidental `chord`/`chords`.

SplitWords.description: Finds missing spaces in improper compound words.

Starving.description: Encourages vivid writing by suggesting `starving` instead of weaker expressions like `very hungry.`

StateOfTheArt.description: Detects incorrect usage of `state of art` and suggests `state of the art` as the correct phrase.

StatuteOfLimitations.description: Corrects `statue of limitations` to `statute of limitations`.

Straightforward.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `straightforward`.

StrikeChord.description: The phrase about resonating with someone is spelled with a chord, not a cord, so fix the typo and keep the idiom intact.

StrikeOfGenius.description: Detects incorrect usage of `strike of genius` and suggests `stroke of genius` as the correct phrase.

StrikeOfLuck.description: Detects incorrect usage of `strike of luck` and suggests `stroke of luck` as the correct phrase.

SubjectAndObjectPronoun.description: Standardizes `subjective pronoun` and `objective pronoun` to the more common `subject -` and `object -`.

SubjectPronoun.description: Fixes sentences that start with `me and X` by putting the proper noun first and using `I`.

SubjunctiveWasToWere.description: Ensures proper use of the subjunctive mood in counterfactual conditional statements starting with `if only` or `I wish`.

SufficeItToSay.description: Corrects `suffice to say` to `suffice it to say`.

SummarySummery.description: Checks for the common confusion between `summary` and `summery`.

SupposedTo.description: Fixes `suppose to` to the correct `supposed to`.

Surreality.description: Suggests changing `surrealness` to the more standard `surreality`.

TakeALookTo.description: Corrects `take a look to`/`have a look to` to correctly use `at`.

TakeCareOf.description: Corrects `take care about` to `take care of`.

TakeControlOf.description: Corrects `take control over` to `take control of`.

TakeItPersonally.description: Corrects `take it personal` to `take it personally`.

TakeMedicine.description: Encourages pairing medicine-related nouns with verbs like `take` or `swallow` instead of `eat`.

TakePrideIn.description: Corrects `take pride of` to `take pride in`.

Tenfold.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `tenfold`.

ThanksALot.description: Corrects the missing article in `thanks lot`, forming `thanks a lot`.

ThatChallenged.description: Corrects `the challenged` to `that challenged` for proper relative clause usage.

ThatThan.description: Corrects the typo `that` to `than` in comparisons.

ThatThis.description: Fixes `the this` to the correct phrase `that this`.

ThatWhich.description: Repeating the word "that" is often redundant. The phrase `that which` is easier to read.

The.description: Fixes especially common misspellings of the word `the`

TheDifferenceBetween.description: Corrects `the different(s) between to `the difference between`.

TheEntiretyOf.description: Corrects `the entire of` to `the entirety of`.

TheHowWhy.description: Removes the extra `the` from expressions like `the how`, skipping `how to` and `who's who`.

TheLastDays.description: Corrects `in the last days` to `in the last few days` and related errors.

TheMy.description: Flags the definite article used together with a possessive.

ThePointFor.description: Corrects `the point for` to `the point of`

TheProperNounPossessive.description: Checks for redundant `the` before possessive proper noun such as `The London's population`.

TheTheToThatThe.description: Corrects `the the` to `that the` or to a single `the`.

TheWhetherWeather.description: Fixes the common mix-up where `whether` is used after `the` when the weather noun is intended.

TheirToThere.description: Corrects `their` when the intended meaning is `there`.

TheirToTheyre.description: Corrects `their` when the intended meaning is `they're`.

Themself.description: Corrects `their self` and `their selves` to `themself` and `themselves`.

There.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `there`.

ThereAfterCompound.description: Normalizes split `there after` to the closed form in adverbial contexts.

ThereIsAgreement.description: Checks for `is there` and its variants agreeing with singular vs plural subjects

ThereMissingIsClause.description: Inserts `is` in common subordinate clauses like `if there a ...` where the copula is omitted.

ThereOwn.description: Corrects `there own`, `they're own`, and `theyre own` to `their own`.

ThereToTheir.description: Corrects `there` when the intended meaning is `their`.

Therefore.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `therefore`.

Therein.description: Flags occurrences of `there in` or `there-in` that should be the closed compound word `therein`.

Theres.description: Replaces the mistaken possessive `their's` before a determiner with the contraction `there's`.

Thereupon.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `thereupon`.

ThesesThese.description: Corrects the common misspelling of `these` as `theses`.

TheyToThem.description: Converts `they` to `them` whenever the pronoun serves as an object after common prepositions or actions that take direct objects.

TheyreConfusions.description: Detects apostrophe and locative edge cases that are awkward to model with standard contraction checks.

TheyreToTheir.description: Corrects `they're` when the intended meaning is `their`.

ThieveNoun.description: Fixes accidental `thieve` in noun phrases where singular `thief` is intended.

ThingThink.description: Corrects the typo `thing` when it should be `think`.

ThinkKnowOff.description: Fixes the common preposition mix-up after verbs like `know` and `think` in phrases such as `know off` and `thought off` when a following token indicates the intended meaning is `of`.

ThisTypeOfThing.description: Checks that the parts of `this/these type(s) of thing(s)` agree in grammatical number

ThoughThought.description: Corrects `though` when it's a typo for `thought`.

ThreatenVerb.description: Normalize `threat` to `threaten` when it is used after modals (or their contractions) because the noun form is being mistaken for a verb.

ThriveOn.description: Corrects `thrive off` and `thrive off of` to `thrive on`.

ThrowAway.description: Finds the typo `through away` and suggests `throw away` or `threw away` instead.

ThrowBabyWithBathwater.description: Corrects wrong or nonstandard variants of the idiom 'to throw the baby out with the bathwater'

ThrowRubbish.description: Checks for throwing rubbish rather than throwing it away.

TickingTimeClock.description: Corrects `ticking time clock` to `ticking time bomb` for idiomatic urgency or `ticking clock` otherwise.

TillDate.description: Corrects the Indian English `till date` to `to date` when Indian English is not the selected dialect.

ToAdverb.description: Flags duplicated `to` around certain adverbs (e.g. `to never to`) and offers fixes that keep only one `to`.

ToBackOut.description: Treats `to backout` as a mistyped infinitive and prefers the two-word verb.

ToGreatLengths.description: Corrects `through great lengths` to `to great lengths`.

ToLoseTooLoose.description: Corrects mixing up `to` with `too` and `lose` with `loose`.

ToNoAvail.description: A collection of linters that can be run as one.

ToSomeDegree.description: Corrects `in some degree` to `to some degree`, meaning to a certain extent.

ToTheMannerBorn.description: Corrects `to the manor born` to `to the manner born`, ensuring the intended meaning of being naturally suited to a way of life.

ToTo.description: Corrects the typo `to to` by either removing the duplication or changing it to `to do`.

ToWorryAbout.description: Fixes incorrect use of `to worried about`.

TomorrowPossessiveModifier.description: Flags `tomorrows` in attributive contexts and suggests the possessive form instead.

TongueInCheek.description: Corrects the idiom when `and` replaces the needed preposition.

ToteTout.description: Flags places where `tote` and `tout` may be confused.

Touristic.description: Suggests replacing the uncommon word `touristic` with `tourist`, `tourism`, and/or `touristy`.

Tradeoff.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `tradeoff`.

TransposedSpace.description: Looks for a space one character too early or too late between words.

TrueToWord.description: Normalizes phrasing around `true to <possessive>` so it follows the conventional `true to one's word`.

TrustIn.description: Detects the wrong preposition in `have trust for`.

TruthToTheFact.description: Flags the redundant phrase `truth to the fact`.

TryOnesHandAt.description: Corrects `try one's hands at` to `try one's hand at`.

TryOnesLuck.description: Corrects `try out one’s luck` to `try one’s luck`

TuffEnough.description: The adjective `tough` pairs with words like `enough` or `like`, so correct the common typo `tuff` in those constructions.

TumblrNames.description: Ensure proper capitalization of Tumblr-related terms.

TurnItOff.description: Fixes the mistake in the phrase `turn it off`.

USUniversities.description: Ensure proper capitalization of major universities in the United States.

UnclosedQuotes.description: Quotation marks should always be closed. Unpaired quotation marks are a hallmark of sloppy work.

Underclock.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `underclock`.

UnitedOrganizations.description: When referring to national or international organizations, make sure to treat them as a proper noun.

UpdatePlaceNames.description: This rule looks for deprecated place names and offers to update them.

Upset.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `upset`.

Upward.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `upward`.

UseEllipsisCharacter.description: Replaces three-period ellipses with the single Unicode ellipsis character.

UseTitleCase.description: Prompts you to use title case in relevant headings.

UseToUsedTo.description: Corrects `use to` to `used to` when meaning accustomed to (after forms of `be` or `get`).

VerbToAdjective.description: Looks for article-led gerund noun phrases like `a fully accounting of`, where an adjective is more likely than an adverb.

VerseAsVerb.description: Corrects the nonstandard use of `verse` as a verb (from `versus`) to standard alternatives.

VeryKnown.description: `very well-known` (or `well-known`) is the standard way to describe something widely recognized, so we flag the uncommon `very known` word pair.

VeryLess.description: Corrects adverbs of degree (`too`, `very`, etc.) used with `less` mostly in the writing of native German speakers.`

VeryMuchSo.description: `Very much` already intensifies the verb, so the trailing `so` is redundant. `Very much so` only reads correctly when the `so` refers back to something earlier, as in the reply `Yes, very much so.`

VeryUnique.description: Flags phrases like `very unique`, `pretty unique`, etc., and suggests using `unique` alone or a more precise adjective such as `special`, `rare`, or `unusual`.

ViciousCircle.description: Corrects and standardizes common errors and variants of `vicious/virtuous circle`.

ViciousCycle.description: Corrects and standardizes common errors and variants of `vicious/virtuous cycle`.

Wanna.description: Corrects the informal contractions `gonna`, `gotta`, and `wanna` to their full forms.

WantBe.description: Detects incorrect usage of `want be` and suggests `won't be` or `want to be` based on context.

WasAloud.description: Ensures `was aloud` and `were aloud` are corrected to `was allowed` or `were allowed` when referring to permission.

WasComprisedOf.description: Rewrites the fixed phrase `was comprised of` to a more widely accepted form.

WaveFunction.description: Identifies the mistake of merging `wave` and `function` into one word. In quantum mechanics, a `wave function` (written as two words) describes the mathematical function that represents the quantum state of a particle or system. Correct usage is crucial for clear and accurate scientific communication.

WayTooAdjective.description: Replaces the preposition `to` with the adverb `too` after `way` when followed by an adjective (e.g. `way too fast`)

WellKept.description: Flags `highly-kept` and recommends `well-kept` as an alternative.

WentAheadAndAgreement.description: Checks for `went ahead and` followed by a present tense verb, which should be past tense.

Whereas.description: The Whereas rule is designed to identify instances where the phrase `where as` is used in text and suggests replacing it with the single word `whereas`.

Whereupon.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `whereupon`.

WhetYourAppetite.description: Ensures `whet your appetite` is used correctly, distinguishing it from the incorrect `wet` variation.

WholeEntire.description: Corrects the redundancy in `whole entire` to `whole` or `entire`.

WhomSubjectOfVerb.description: Detects whom and its variants used as the subject of a verb instead of who.

WidelyAccepted.description: Flags `wide accepted`, `wide acceptable`, or `wide used` and recommends switching `wide` to the adverb `widely`.

Widespread.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `widespread`.

WillContain.description: Incorrect verb form: `will` should be followed by the base form `contain`.

WillGonna.description: Corrects the redundant `will gonna` and `will going to` to `will`.

WillNonLemma.description: Flags wrong verb forms after `will` or `shall`

WinPrize.description: Catches the mix-up between `price`/`prise` and `prize` after the verb `win`.

WishCould.description: Checks for `can` being used after `wish` when it should be `could`.

WithOpenArms.description: Corrects wrong variants of the idiom `welcome/greet with open arms`.

Without.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `without`.

WithoutOut.description: When writers accidentally type `without out`, Harper can collapse the two words back into the single preposition.

WokVerbTypo.description: Flags likely typo cases where `wok` appears where the verb `work` is expected.

WordPressDotcom.description: Ensures correct capitalization of WordPress.com. This rule verifies that the official stylization of WordPress.com is used when referring to the hosting provider.

Worldwide.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `worldwide`.

WorseOrWorst.description: Corrects `worse` and `worst` used in contexts where the other belongs.

WorstCaseScenario.description: Corrects `worst-case scenario` when the hyphen is missing or `worse` is used instead of `worst`.

WorthToDo.description: Corrects `worth to` + a verb to `worth` + the gerund of the verb.

Worthwhile.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `worthwhile`.

WouldNeverHave.description: Corrects `would/could have never` to `never would/could have`.

WreakHavoc.description: Corrects the eggcorn `wreck havoc` to `wreak havoc`, which is the proper term for causing chaos or destruction.

WrongApostrophe.description: Corrects semicolons, acute accents, and backticks typed instead of apostrophes.

WrongNegative.description: If an unknown word looks like it might be a negative word, suggests correct words that are in the dictionary.

WroughtIron.description: `Wrought iron` is low-carbon, malleable iron used for decorative work; variants like `rod iron` or `rot iron` are phonetic misspellings that may confuse readers.

YourOutClauseAgreement.description: Corrects `your` when it appears where a subject-plus-verb contraction is intended before `out` and a following preposition.

YourPredicateAdjective.description: Catches cases where a predicate adjective follows `your`, `yr`, `ur`, or `ya` and suggests the proper contraction so the sentence states how someone is feeling or behaving.

Yourself.description: Looks for incorrect spacing inside the closed compound `yourself`, while skipping hyphenated `self-...` compounds.
